newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analyst raises EU grain forecast to 198.9 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Analyst raises EU grain forecast to 198.9 mln T.

text.p: Private cereals analyst Strategie Grains on Monday revised its forecast for the 1996 European Union grain crop by 5.2 million tonnes to 198.9 million tonnes.

It said the decision to raise its previous forecast of 193.7 million tonnes came after good yield reports in northwest Europe and pointed to a 13 percent gain from last year's harvest of 176.5 million tonnes.
Strategie Grains, based near Paris, predicted a soft wheat crop for the 15-nation bloc of 88.1 million tonnes, up 10 percent from last year.

It estimated barley production at 52.5 million tonnes, up 20 percent from 1995, and maize at 32.9 million, up 11 percent. It pegged durum production at 7.8 million tonnes, up 16 percent, and rye at 5.4 million, down 12 percent.

"The increase (in forecast total grain production) from last month is due to wheat and barley yields, especially in France and Britain, and barley in Denmark," Strategie Grains said in a monthly report.
The Strategie Grains estimates have tended to be at the high end of private and government forecasts this year.
But its new predictions are the latest in a series of record crop predictions after strong yields in northern and southern Europe wiped out the effects of drought in central France.
French cereals office ONIC said last week it expected the EU grain harvest -- now accounting for 15 countries instead of 12 -- to exceed the 1991 record of 194.8 million tonnes.
Austria, Finland and Sweden joined the EU last year.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture predicts an EU grain harvest of 197.8 million tonnes this year.
